title: Fallback priority drift detection and autorepair playbook
creator: Evan Brooks
description:
Summary: During a recent global capacity migration we observed repeated mis-selection of model variants and cross-region reroutes for a subset of production traffic. Root cause analysis shows a subtle 'fallback priority drift' where ephemeral updates to policy weights were applied out-of-order between the control plane and the serving layers, causing different router shards to have conflicting priority views and triggering oscillatory reroutes when capacity thresholds changed. This ticket tracks detection, automated repair, and long-term safeguards to prevent recurrence.

Impact: ~12% of requests for two customer tiers experienced increased latency as traffic bounced across regions; several tail-heavy jobs incurred higher token-cost due to repeated re-encoding and KV cache misses. No data loss or model inference corruption was observed.

Root cause (short): Control-plane policy delta pushes used a best-effort fanout with eventual reconciliation. During a capacity migration we had a window where some router shards applied new per-variant priorities while others still used older priorities. The mismatch combined with a conservative capacity predictor to mark local pool as underprovisioned, which triggered regional failover. The mismatch caused some requests to flip between variants and regions until a stale policy snapshot was reconciled.

Why this was missed: Existing monitoring focused on absolute error rates and infra capacity but did not alert on intra-policy divergence (i.e., per-shard policy checksum mismatch). The current reconciliation job runs on a 15m cadence which is too slow for bursty policy churn during migrations.

Goals: 1) Detect policy drift within 30s of divergence. 2) Provide an autorepair playbook that can safely force-consistent reconciliation without unsafe failovers. 3) Harden rollout logic so variant priorities are applied atomically or with safe feature gates. 4) Add pre-migration checks and canaries for policy pushes and support automated rollback to last-known-good policy on detected drift.

Deliverables: detailed detection rules, a reconciliation controller that supports safe repair and circuit-breaking, runbook updates for on-call, a small control-plane change to add policy version vectors, an integration test harness that simulates staggered shard updates, and dashboards/alerts for drift metrics.
comments: 2026-03-02 - initial incident triage: SRE and routing owners confirmed oscillation pattern; created temporary rate-limit-based mitigation to reduce reroute amplification (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/2143).
2026-03-04 - RCA meeting: determined root cause as asynchronous policy application + slow reconciliation (notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/Routing/Fallback+Priority+Drift+RCA).

2026-03-05 - Detection prototype: added per-shard policy checksum emission to router telemetry (Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd1234/policy-drift). Observed drift windows align with capacity push windows.

2026-03-06 - Design review: decided on version-vector metadata for policy deltas and a lightweight reconciliation controller that prefers convergence over immediate forced rollback in high-traffic shards. Feedback from Marco Nguyen: ensure controller has an aggressive dry-run mode and an emergency force-rollback toggle.
2026-03-08 - Implementation: started controller and reconciliation worker (WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/558). Added unit tests for version-vector comparisons.
2026-03-09 - Runbook draft: added 'Detect drift -> Pause policy pushes -> Reconcile -> Canary' steps; reviewed by SRE. Action item: add exact Grafana alert thresholds and Slack incident hook.

2026-03-10 - Integration tests: added a harness to simulate staggered shard updates and injected capacity migration events (test job: https://ci.redwood.com/job/routing-reconcile/342). Found edge case where reconciliation could race with in-flight request routing; added a brief pinning window to avoid double-apply.
2026-03-12 - Security review: scoped and set to 'not required' for controller code path (no customer data access).
2026-03-12 - Next: finish PR, run extended canary in staging against a traffic-generator and schedule follow-up rollout for runtime-2.4 canary lane. Assigned owners for each action item below.
action_items: AI-1: Add per-shard policy checksum and expose drift metric (owner: Priya Iyer, due: 2026-03-15) - dashboard & alert (SLO: detect within 30s).
AI-2: Implement reconciliation controller with safe modes: dry-run, staged-apply, emergency-force (owner: Marco Nguyen, due: 2026-03-22) - PR: control-plane#558
AI-3: Introduce policy version-vector and ordering guarantees for push protocol (owner: Lydia Chen, due: 2026-03-18) - design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/Routing/Policy+Versioning
AI-4: Shorten reconciliation cadence from 15m to 30s during migrations and add migration-aware sampler (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-03-20).
AI-5: Build integration test that flips policies on a subset of shards and verifies no oscillatory reroute (owner: QA - Diego Alvarez, estimate: 3 points, due: 2026-03-19).
AI-6: Update runbooks and run a fire-drill with on-call to exercise detect-and-reconcile (owner: Runbook WG - Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-24).
AI-7: Add canary gating for capacity migrations: require 5-minute stable policy checksum before draining or moving capacity (owner: Capacity PM - Rahul Singh, due: 2026-03-21).
AI-8: Add metric tracking for extra cost amplification (token re-generation due to reroute) and alert when >2% across customer tiers (owner: Data Eng - Noor Malik, due: 2026-03-25).
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for version-vector & reconciliation logic. 2) Integration harness simulating staggered shard updates and capacity pushes. 3) Staging canary: deploy controller in dry-run against traffic generator for 72h, then staged-apply to 5% of production-like traffic. 4) Failure injection: simulate delayed push and confirm controller detects and repairs without increasing error rate. 5) Post-rollout validation: check policy checksum convergence, percent reroute reduction, and cost amplification metrics.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: feature-flagged deploy to control-plane + router checksum emission (staging). Stage 2: enable reconciliation dry-run for 7 days against synthetic traffic. Stage 3: canary apply to 5% live traffic and monitor for 24h. Stage 4: full rollout with emergency rollback policy and on-call watch for 48h. Communication: announce to customers via status page if canary exposes customer-visible regressions.
